title: Gupta Empire
capsule: The Gupta Empire was an Indian dynastic state founded c. 320 AD when Chandragupta I (r. c. 319–335) assumed the title maharajadhiraja (Great King of Kings) in Magadha and expanded through marriage alliance with the Licchavis of Nepal. Under Samudragupta (r. c. 335–375), whose Allahabad Pillar inscription records campaigns across northern India and tributary relationships with southern kings, and Chandragupta II (r. c. 375–415), the empire reached its greatest extent, stretching from the Bengal delta to the Punjab and from the Himalayas to the Narmada River. The late 5th century brought repeated Huna (Hephthalite) invasions: Skandagupta repelled the first incursion c. 455, but subsequent attacks fragmented the empire and by c. 550 Gupta authority had collapsed into regional successor states.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Gupta core territory is well-attested through copper-plate land grants and stone inscriptions with provenance; peripheral regions, particularly the Deccan and the western borderlands, are inferred from tributary lists in the Allahabad Pillar inscription and carry considerable uncertainty.
